Commentary of al-Shawkani (*Fath al-Qadir*) on surah 15, verses 16–44 (part 1 of 2):

When He, glorified is He, mentioned the disbelief of the disbelievers and the incapacity of them and of their idols, He mentioned His dazzling power and His wondrous creation, so that they might infer His oneness from it. So He said: ﴿And We have certainly placed in the sky constellations of stars﴾. The verb *ja'ala* (placed/made) — if it means *khalaqa* (created), then *fi al-sama'* (in the sky) is connected to it; if it means *sayyara* (rendered, made into), then *fi al-sama'* is its predicate. *Al-buruj* (the constellations/mansions) in the language means palaces and dwellings, and what is meant here are the mansions of the sun, the moon and the wandering stars, which are the well-known twelve, as experience indicates. The Arabs consider knowledge of the positions of the stars and their mansions to be among the most noble sciences, and they use them to find their way, to know the times, and to know fertility and drought. They said: the celestial sphere has twelve *burj*s, and the names of these *buruj* are: Aries (*al-Hamal*), Taurus (*al-Thawr*), Gemini (*al-Jawza'*), Cancer (*al-Saratan*), Leo (*al-Asad*), Virgo (*al-Sunbulah*), Libra (*al-Mizan*), Scorpio (*al-'Aqrab*), Sagittarius (*al-Qaws*), Capricorn (*al-Jady*), Aquarius (*al-Dalw*), Pisces (*al-Hut*).

Each three of them are of the nature of one of the four elements, among those who occupy themselves with this science. They call Aries, Leo and Sagittarius the "fiery trigon"; Taurus, Virgo and Capricorn the "earthy trigon"; Gemini, Libra and Aquarius the "airy trigon"; and Cancer, Scorpio and Pisces the "watery trigon."

The root of *al-buruj* is *al-zuhur* (manifestation), and from it comes *tabarruj al-mar'ah* (a woman's displaying of her adornment).

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: *al-buruj* are the stars, and they were so called because of their manifestness and their elevation. It was also said: they are the seven wandering stars among them; this was said by Abu Salih. It was also said: they are palaces and houses in the sky, in which there are guards. The pronoun in *wa-zayyannaha* (and We adorned it) refers to the sky; that is, and We adorned the sky with the sun, the moon, the stars and the constellations, for the onlookers who look at it, or for the reflecting, heedful ones who infer, if it is from *al-nazar*, which is inference.

﴿And We guarded it﴾, that is, the sky, ﴿from every accursed devil﴾. Abu 'Ubaydah said: *al-rajim* means the one stoned with stars, as in His saying: ﴿missiles against the devils﴾ [al-Mulk: 5]. *Al-rajm* in the language is throwing stones; then it was used for cursing, expelling and distancing, *rajm*, because throwing stones entails these meanings.

﴿Except one who steals a hearing﴾. This is an exception that is *muttasil* (connected), that is, except from among those who steal a hearing. It may also be *munqati'* (disconnected), that is, but whoever steals a hearing, then a clear flaming fire pursues him. The meaning: We guarded the sky from the devils, so that they would not hear anything of the revelation or other things, except that one who steals a hearing, then the meteors pursue him and kill him or harm him. The meaning of *fa-atba'ahu* is that he followed him, overtook him, or caught up with him.

*Al-shihab* is the star or the blazing, shining fire, as in His saying: ﴿with a burning brand﴾ [al-Naml: 7]. Dhu al-Rummah said:

*"As if it were a star in pursuit of a demon."*

The star was called *shihab* because of its brightness, resembling fire. *Al-mubin* means evident to those who see; they see it and it is not obscured to them.

Al-Qurtubi said: It has been disputed whether the *shihab* kills or not. Ibn 'Abbas said: the *shihab* wounds, burns and harms, but does not kill. Al-Hasan and a group said: it kills.

Based on this view, regarding their being killed by the meteors before they have conveyed the hearing to the jinn, there are two opinions. The first: they are killed before they pass on to others what they have stolen by hearing, so the news of the heavens does not reach anyone other than the prophets; and for this reason soothsaying has ceased.

The second: they are killed after they have passed on what they stole by hearing to other jinn. He said: Al-Mawardi mentioned this, then said: the first view is more sound.

He said: It has been disputed whether there was hurling of meteors before the mission (*al-mab'ath*). Most said: yes. It was said: no, rather that happened only after the mission.

Al-Zajjaj said: The hurling of meteors is one of the signs of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, among the things that happened after his birth, because the poets in ancient times did not mention it in their poetry.

Many of the people of knowledge said: we see the shooting of stars, so it is possible that this is as we see it; then it becomes fire when it overtakes the devil. It is also possible to say that they are pelted with a flame of fire of the air, and so it appears to us that it is a star that is gliding.

﴿And the earth — We spread it out﴾, that is, We stretched it out and laid it out flat, as in His saying: ﴿and the earth, after that, He spread it out﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 30], and in His saying: ﴿and We laid out the earth, and how excellent are the Spreaders﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 48]. In this there is a refutation of whoever claims that it is like a sphere. ﴿And We cast into it firm mountains﴾, that is, mountains firmly fixed, lest it shake with its inhabitants. The explanation of this has already been given in surah al-Ra'd. ﴿And We caused to grow in it of everything weighed﴾, that is, We caused to grow in the earth of everything determined and known. He expressed this by *al-wazn* (weighing), because it is a measure by which things are known. From this is the saying of the poet:

*"Before your meeting I was one of strength; for every adversary, his balance is with me."*

It was also said: the meaning of *mawzun* is divided (*maqsum*); it was also said: counted (*ma'dud*). The intended purpose of the affirmation is origination and bringing into existence. It was also said: the pronoun refers to the mountains; that is, We caused to grow in the mountains of everything weighed: of gold, silver, copper, lead and the like. It was also said: *mawzun* is weighed by the balance of wisdom and determined by the measure of need. It was also said: *al-mawzun* is that whose goodness is judged, as one says *kalam mawzun*, that is, good speech.

﴿And We made for you therein means of livelihood﴾, by which you live, of foods and drinks; *ma'ayish* is the plural of *ma'isha*. It was said: they are garments. It was said: they are the management of the causes of provision for the duration of life. Al-Mawardi said: this is the apparent meaning.

I say: rather the first view is more apparent. From this is the saying of Jarir:

*"You burden me with the livelihood of the family of Zayd, and who for me [will provide] the thin bread and the lizard?"*

﴿And [also] those for whom you are not providers﴾ is coordinated with *ma'ayish* (means of livelihood); that is, We made for you therein means of livelihood, and [We made therein] for those for whom you are not providers: they are the slaves, the servants and the children, whose true provider is Allah, even if some of the servants think that he is the provider for them by virtue of his independent earning. It is also permissible for it to be coordinated with the position (*mahall*) of *lakum* (for you); that is, We made for you therein means of livelihood, and We made for those for whom you are not providers therein means of livelihood, and these are those previously mentioned, and this includes the animals of various kinds. It is not permissible to coordinate with the pronoun in *lakum* in the genitive, because according to most grammarians it is not permissible except by repeating the preposition. It was also said: he meant the wild animals.

﴿And there is not a thing but that with Us are its treasuries﴾. *In* (إن) is the negating particle, and *min* (مِن) is extra for emphasis. This construction is general, because an indefinite noun falls within the scope of negation together with the addition of *min*, and with the word *shay'* (thing), which encompasses all existents and applies to each individual among them. Thus it conveys that all things are, with Allah, in His treasuries; nothing goes out of them. *Al-khaza'in* is the plural of *khizanah*, which is the place in which precious things are kept. The mention of treasuries is an illustration of His capacity over every possible thing. The meaning: all possibilities are within His power and under His possession, which He brings from non-existence into existence in a measure as He wills.

Most of the exegetes said: what is meant in this verse is rain, because it is the cause of provisions and livelihoods. It was said: *al-khaza'in* are the keys; that is, there is not a thing but that with Us in the sky are its keys. The better view is what we have mentioned, namely the generality for every existent; indeed the word *shay'* may apply to the non-existent, according to the well-known disagreement on this matter.

﴿And We do not send it down except in a known measure﴾, that is, We do not send it down from the sky to the earth, or bring it into existence for the servants, except in a known measure. *Al-qadar* means the quantity. The meaning: Allah, glorified is He, does not bring into existence for the servants any of those things mentioned except accompanied by that bringing-into-existence in a specific measure, according to what His will requires, in proportion to the servants' need for it, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And if Allah had extended provision for His servants, they would have transgressed in the earth; but He sends down in measure what He wills﴾ [al-Shura: 27]. The sending down has been explained as giving, and explained as creating, and explained as bringing into existence; the meanings are close. The clause ﴿and We do not send it down﴾ is coordinated with an implied clause, that is: and there is not a thing but with Us are its treasuries, We send it down, and We do not send it down, or it is in the position of an accusative of circumstance (*hal*).

﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing﴾ is coordinated with ﴿And We made for you therein means of livelihood﴾, and what is between them is a parenthetical insertion.

Hamzah read *al-rih* (the wind) in the singular. The others read *al-riyah* (the winds) in the plural. On the reading of Hamzah, the definite article in *al-rih* is for the category (*li-l-jins*).

Al-Azhari said: He made the winds *lawaqih* (fertilizing) because they carry the clouds, that is, they bear them and turn them, then they pass over with them and cause them to descend. Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿until, when they have borne heavy clouds﴾ [al-A'raf: 57], that is, carried them. A she-camel is *laqih* when she has conceived the fetus in her womb. Al-Farra' and Ibn Qutaybah said this. It was also said: *lawaqih* means *mulaqqihah* (causing to fertilize). Ibn al-Anbari said: the Arabs say *abqala al-nabt fa-huwa baqil*, that is, *mubqil* (the plant has put forth green growth, so it is a green plant). The meaning: they fertilize the trees, that is, by their power. It was also said: the meaning of *lawaqih* is "possessing fertilization" (*dhawat laqah*). Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is "and possessing a bearing-state" (*dhat liqhah*), because they squeeze the clouds and milk them as a milk-camel is milked. One says *ramih*, that is, possessing a spear; *labin*, that is, possessing milk; and *tamir*, that is, possessing dates. Abu 'Ubaydah said: *lawaqih* means *malaqih*; he went to the view that it is the plural of *malqahah*.

In this verse there is a comparison of the winds that carry water to a pregnant woman, and of the fertilization of trees to the impregnation of a pregnancy.

﴿And We sent down from the sky water﴾, that is, from the clouds. Everything that is above you and shades you is *sama'* (sky). It was also said: from the direction of the sky. The water here means rain water. ﴿And We gave it to you to drink﴾, that is, We made that rain for your watering, and for the drinking of your livestock and your land. Abu 'Ali said: one says *saqaytuhu al-ma'* when you give him an amount that quenches his thirst, and *asqaytuhu nahran*, that is, you made it a drinking place for him. On this basis, *asqaynakumuhu* is more emphatic than *saqaynakumuhu*. It was also said: *saqa* and *asqa* have one meaning. ﴿And you are not its keepers﴾, that is, its treasuries are not with you; rather its treasuries are with Us, and We are the keepers of it. Thus He, glorified is He, negated from them what He had affirmed for Himself in His saying: ﴿And there is not a thing but that with Us are its treasuries﴾. It was also said: the meaning is: you are not its keepers after We have sent it down upon you, that is, you cannot preserve it in wells, pools and springs; rather We are the ones who preserve it therein, so that it may be a store for you when you are in need of it.

﴿And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death﴾, that is, We bring life into existence in created beings and strip it from them whenever We wish. The purpose of this is to infer from these matters the perfection of His power, mighty and majestic is He, and that He is capable of resurrection, rising, and recompense to His servants according to what they deserve and what His will requires. For this reason He said: ﴿And We are the inheritors﴾, that is, of the earth and of whoever is upon it, because He, glorified is He, is the one who remains after the perishing of His creation, the Living who does not die, the Everlasting whose existence does not cease. ﴿And to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth﴾ [Al 'Imran: 180].

﴿And We have certainly known those who precede among you﴾. This *lam* is the one preparing for an oath (*al-lam al-muwatti'ah lil-qasam*), and likewise the *lam* in ﴿And We have certainly known those who delay﴾. What is meant by those who precede is those who precede in birth and death, and those who delay in them. It was said: those who precede in obedience and those who delay in it. It was said: those who precede in the battle line and those who delay. It was said: what is meant by those who precede are the dead, and by those who delay are the living. It was said: those who precede are the earlier nations before the community of Muhammad, and those who delay are the community of Muhammad. It was said: those who precede are those who were killed in jihad, and those who delay are those who were not killed.

﴿And indeed your Lord — it is He who will gather them﴾, that is, He is the one who takes charge of that, the one capable of it, to the exclusion of others, as the pronoun of separation (*damir al-fasl*) indicates by way of restriction. In it is [the indication] that He, glorified is He, will recompense the doer of good for his goodness and the doer of evil for his evil, because this is the very purpose of gathering. ﴿Indeed, He is Wise﴾, who conducts affairs according to what His far-reaching wisdom requires. ﴿Knowing﴾, whose knowledge encompasses all things, nothing being hidden from Him of them; and whoever is so, has far-reaching power over everything within the scope of His knowledge, (p-760) and His judgment proceeds in it, glorified is He; there is no god but Him.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿And We have certainly placed in the sky constellations of stars﴾, that he said: "Stars."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah the same (as above).

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Abu Salih, who said: "The great stars."

He also related from Atiyyah, who said: "Palaces in the sky, in which are the guards."

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah: "al-Rajim (the accursed one): the one cursed."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Except one who steals a hearing﴾, that he meant he wished to snatch the hearing, like His saying: ﴿Except one who snatches a snatching﴾ [al-Saffat: 10].

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Dahhak, who said: Ibn Abbas used to say that the shooting stars do not kill, but they burn, cause insanity (yakhbil) and wound, without killing.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from him regarding His saying: ﴿And We caused to grow therein of every thing weighed (mawzun)﴾, that he said: "Known (ma'lum)."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also, regarding ﴿of every thing weighed﴾, he said: "By measure (bi-qadar)."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Zayd, who said: "The things that are weighed."

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ikrimah, who said: "What the mountains cause to grow, like kohl and its like."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿And whom you are not providing for (lahu bi-raziqin)﴾, that he said: "The beasts and the livestock."

These same (narrators) related from Mansur, who said: "The wild animals."

al-Bazzar, Ibn Mardawayh and Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azamah related from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The treasuries of Allah are speech; when He wills a thing, He says to it 'Be,' and it is."

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn Jurayj regarding His saying: ﴿But with Us are its treasuries﴾, that he said: "Rain specifically."

Ibn al-Mundhir related from Mujahid something similar.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Rain has not decreased since Allah sent it down, but one land receives more rain than another," then he recited: ﴿And We do not send it down except in a known measure﴾.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "No year is rainier than another year, but Allah turns it wherever He wills," then he recited: ﴿And there is not a thing but its treasuries are with Us, and We do not send it down except in a known measure﴾.

Ibn Mardawayh related it from him as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) report.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Tabarani related from Ibn Mas'ud regarding His saying: ﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing (lawaqih)﴾, that he said: "Allah sends the wind, and it carries the water and fertilizes the clouds with it, so they yield milk as a she-camel yields milk, and then it rains."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azamah related something similar from Ibn Abbas.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related from Ubayd ibn Umayr, who said: "Allah sends the bearers of glad tidings (al-mubashshirah), and they sweep over the earth with a sweep. Then He sends the stirrers (al-muthirah), which stir up the clouds and make them into fragments (kisaf). Then He sends the gatherers (al-mu'allifah), which gather them together and make them a heap (rukam). Then He sends the fertilizers (al-lawaqih), which fertilize them, and it rains."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azamah, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Daylami related with a weak chain from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The southern wind is from Paradise, and it is the fertilizing wind which Allah mentioned in His Book."

al-Tayalisi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Hibban, al-Tabarani and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, related from Ibn Abbas, who said: "A woman used to pray behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), a beautiful one among the most beautiful of women. Some of the people would advance so as to be in the first row, lest they see her, and some would hold back so as to be in the last row. When she bowed, they would look from beneath their armpits. So Allah revealed: ﴿And We have certainly known those who go before among you, and We have certainly known those who remain behind﴾." This hadith is from the narration of Abu al-Jawza' from Ibn Abbas.

Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn al-Mundhir related it as a statement of Abu al-Jawza'. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is more likely to be the sound (asahh)."

Ibn Kathir said: "In this hadith there is a severe irregularity (nakarah shadidah)."

al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, that he said: ﴿Those who go before﴾ are the earlier rows, and ﴿those who remain behind﴾ are the later rows.

Many hadiths have been reported that the best rows of men are the first of them and the worst are the last of them, and the best rows of women are the last of them and the worst are the first of them.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ata' and Muqatil ibn Hibban that the verse concerns the rows in battle.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Hasan, who said: "Those who go before in obedience to Allah, and those who remain behind in disobedience to Allah."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Abbas, who said: By "those who go before" is meant whoever has died, and by "those who remain behind" is meant whoever is alive and has not died.

These same (narrators) related from him also, who said: "Those who go before" are Adam and whoever passed on from his descendants, and "those who remain behind" are those still in the loins of men.

Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Qatadah something similar.

﴿And the earth — We spread it out﴾, that is, We stretched it out and laid it out flat, as in His saying: ﴿and the earth, after that, He spread it out﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 30], and in His saying: ﴿and We laid out the earth, and how excellent are the Spreaders﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 48]. In this there is a refutation of whoever claims that it is like a sphere. ﴿And We cast into it firm mountains﴾, that is, mountains firmly fixed, lest it shake with its inhabitants. The explanation of this has already been given in surah al-Ra'd. ﴿And We caused to grow in it of everything weighed﴾, that is, We caused to grow in the earth of everything determined and known. He expressed this by *al-wazn* (weighing), because it is a measure by which things are known. From this is the saying of the poet:

*"Before your meeting I was one of strength; for every adversary, his balance is with me."*

It was also said: the meaning of *mawzun* is divided (*maqsum*); it was also said: counted (*ma'dud*). The intended purpose of the affirmation is origination and bringing into existence. It was also said: the pronoun refers to the mountains; that is, We caused to grow in the mountains of everything weighed: of gold, silver, copper, lead and the like. It was also said: *mawzun* is weighed by the balance of wisdom and determined by the measure of need. It was also said: *al-mawzun* is that whose goodness is judged, as one says *kalam mawzun*, that is, good speech.

﴿And We made for you therein means of livelihood﴾, by which you live, of foods and drinks; *ma'ayish* is the plural of *ma'isha*. It was said: they are garments. It was said: they are the management of the causes of provision for the duration of life. Al-Mawardi said: this is the apparent meaning.

I say: rather the first view is more apparent. From this is the saying of Jarir:

*"You burden me with the livelihood of the family of Zayd, and who for me [will provide] the thin bread and the lizard?"*

﴿And [also] those for whom you are not providers﴾ is coordinated with *ma'ayish* (means of livelihood); that is, We made for you therein means of livelihood, and [We made therein] for those for whom you are not providers: they are the slaves, the servants and the children, whose true provider is Allah, even if some of the servants think that he is the provider for them by virtue of his independent earning. It is also permissible for it to be coordinated with the position (*mahall*) of *lakum* (for you); that is, We made for you therein means of livelihood, and We made for those for whom you are not providers therein means of livelihood, and these are those previously mentioned, and this includes the animals of various kinds. It is not permissible to coordinate with the pronoun in *lakum* in the genitive, because according to most grammarians it is not permissible except by repeating the preposition. It was also said: he meant the wild animals.

﴿And there is not a thing but that with Us are its treasuries﴾. *In* (إن) is the negating particle, and *min* (مِن) is extra for emphasis. This construction is general, because an indefinite noun falls within the scope of negation together with the addition of *min*, and with the word *shay'* (thing), which encompasses all existents and applies to each individual among them. Thus it conveys that all things are, with Allah, in His treasuries; nothing goes out of them. *Al-khaza'in* is the plural of *khizanah*, which is the place in which precious things are kept. The mention of treasuries is an illustration of His capacity over every possible thing. The meaning: all possibilities are within His power and under His possession, which He brings from non-existence into existence in a measure as He wills.

Most of the exegetes said: what is meant in this verse is rain, because it is the cause of provisions and livelihoods. It was said: *al-khaza'in* are the keys; that is, there is not a thing but that with Us in the sky are its keys. The better view is what we have mentioned, namely the generality for every existent; indeed the word *shay'* may apply to the non-existent, according to the well-known disagreement on this matter.

﴿And We do not send it down except in a known measure﴾, that is, We do not send it down from the sky to the earth, or bring it into existence for the servants, except in a known measure. *Al-qadar* means the quantity. The meaning: Allah, glorified is He, does not bring into existence for the servants any of those things mentioned except accompanied by that bringing-into-existence in a specific measure, according to what His will requires, in proportion to the servants' need for it, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And if Allah had extended provision for His servants, they would have transgressed in the earth; but He sends down in measure what He wills﴾ [al-Shura: 27]. The sending down has been explained as giving, and explained as creating, and explained as bringing into existence; the meanings are close. The clause ﴿and We do not send it down﴾ is coordinated with an implied clause, that is: and there is not a thing but with Us are its treasuries, We send it down, and We do not send it down, or it is in the position of an accusative of circumstance (*hal*).

﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing﴾ is coordinated with ﴿And We made for you therein means of livelihood﴾, and what is between them is a parenthetical insertion.

Hamzah read *al-rih* (the wind) in the singular. The others read *al-riyah* (the winds) in the plural. On the reading of Hamzah, the definite article in *al-rih* is for the category (*li-l-jins*).

Al-Azhari said: He made the winds *lawaqih* (fertilizing) because they carry the clouds, that is, they bear them and turn them, then they pass over with them and cause them to descend. Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿until, when they have borne heavy clouds﴾ [al-A'raf: 57], that is, carried them. A she-camel is *laqih* when she has conceived the fetus in her womb. Al-Farra' and Ibn Qutaybah said this. It was also said: *lawaqih* means *mulaqqihah* (causing to fertilize). Ibn al-Anbari said: the Arabs say *abqala al-nabt fa-huwa baqil*, that is, *mubqil* (the plant has put forth green growth, so it is a green plant). The meaning: they fertilize the trees, that is, by their power. It was also said: the meaning of *lawaqih* is "possessing fertilization" (*dhawat laqah*). Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is "and possessing a bearing-state" (*dhat liqhah*), because they squeeze the clouds and milk them as a milk-camel is milked. One says *ramih*, that is, possessing a spear; *labin*, that is, possessing milk; and *tamir*, that is, possessing dates. Abu 'Ubaydah said: *lawaqih* means *malaqih*; he went to the view that it is the plural of *malqahah*.

In this verse there is a comparison of the winds that carry water to a pregnant woman, and of the fertilization of trees to the impregnation of a pregnancy.

﴿And We sent down from the sky water﴾, that is, from the clouds. Everything that is above you and shades you is *sama'* (sky). It was also said: from the direction of the sky. The water here means rain water. ﴿And We gave it to you to drink﴾, that is, We made that rain for your watering, and for the drinking of your livestock and your land. Abu 'Ali said: one says *saqaytuhu al-ma'* when you give him an amount that quenches his thirst, and *asqaytuhu nahran*, that is, you made it a drinking place for him. On this basis, *asqaynakumuhu* is more emphatic than *saqaynakumuhu*. It was also said: *saqa* and *asqa* have one meaning. ﴿And you are not its keepers﴾, that is, its treasuries are not with you; rather its treasuries are with Us, and We are the keepers of it. Thus He, glorified is He, negated from them what He had affirmed for Himself in His saying: ﴿And there is not a thing but that with Us are its treasuries﴾. It was also said: the meaning is: you are not its keepers after We have sent it down upon you, that is, you cannot preserve it in wells, pools and springs; rather We are the ones who preserve it therein, so that it may be a store for you when you are in need of it.

﴿And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death﴾, that is, We bring life into existence in created beings and strip it from them whenever We wish. The purpose of this is to infer from these matters the perfection of His power, mighty and majestic is He, and that He is capable of resurrection, rising, and recompense to His servants according to what they deserve and what His will requires. For this reason He said: ﴿And We are the inheritors﴾, that is, of the earth and of whoever is upon it, because He, glorified is He, is the one who remains after the perishing of His creation, the Living who does not die, the Everlasting whose existence does not cease. ﴿And to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth﴾ [Al 'Imran: 180].

﴿And We have certainly known those who precede among you﴾. This *lam* is the one preparing for an oath (*al-lam al-muwatti'ah lil-qasam*), and likewise the *lam* in ﴿And We have certainly known those who delay﴾. What is meant by those who precede is those who precede in birth and death, and those who delay in them. It was said: those who precede in obedience and those who delay in it. It was said: those who precede in the battle line and those who delay. It was said: what is meant by those who precede are the dead, and by those who delay are the living. It was said: those who precede are the earlier nations before the community of Muhammad, and those who delay are the community of Muhammad. It was said: those who precede are those who were killed in jihad, and those who delay are those who were not killed.

﴿And indeed your Lord — it is He who will gather them﴾, that is, He is the one who takes charge of that, the one capable of it, to the exclusion of others, as the pronoun of separation (*damir al-fasl*) indicates by way of restriction. In it is [the indication] that He, glorified is He, will recompense the doer of good for his goodness and the doer of evil for his evil, because this is the very purpose of gathering. ﴿Indeed, He is Wise﴾, who conducts affairs according to what His far-reaching wisdom requires. ﴿Knowing﴾, whose knowledge encompasses all things, nothing being hidden from Him of them; and whoever is so, has far-reaching power over everything within the scope of His knowledge, (p-760) and His judgment proceeds in it, glorified is He; there is no god but Him.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿And We have certainly placed in the sky constellations of stars﴾, that he said: "Stars."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah the same (as above).

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Abu Salih, who said: "The great stars."

He also related from Atiyyah, who said: "Palaces in the sky, in which are the guards."

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah: "al-Rajim (the accursed one): the one cursed."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Except one who steals a hearing﴾, that he meant he wished to snatch the hearing, like His saying: ﴿Except one who snatches a snatching﴾ [al-Saffat: 10].

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Dahhak, who said: Ibn Abbas used to say that the shooting stars do not kill, but they burn, cause insanity (yakhbil) and wound, without killing.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from him regarding His saying: ﴿And We caused to grow therein of every thing weighed (mawzun)﴾, that he said: "Known (ma'lum)."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also, regarding ﴿of every thing weighed﴾, he said: "By measure (bi-qadar)."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Zayd, who said: "The things that are weighed."

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ikrimah, who said: "What the mountains cause to grow, like kohl and its like."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿And whom you are not providing for (lahu bi-raziqin)﴾, that he said: "The beasts and the livestock."

These same (narrators) related from Mansur, who said: "The wild animals."

al-Bazzar, Ibn Mardawayh and Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azamah related from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The treasuries of Allah are speech; when He wills a thing, He says to it 'Be,' and it is."

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn Jurayj regarding His saying: ﴿But with Us are its treasuries﴾, that he said: "Rain specifically."

Ibn al-Mundhir related from Mujahid something similar.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Rain has not decreased since Allah sent it down, but one land receives more rain than another," then he recited: ﴿And We do not send it down except in a known measure﴾.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "No year is rainier than another year, but Allah turns it wherever He wills," then he recited: ﴿And there is not a thing but its treasuries are with Us, and We do not send it down except in a known measure﴾.

Ibn Mardawayh related it from him as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) report.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Tabarani related from Ibn Mas'ud regarding His saying: ﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing (lawaqih)﴾, that he said: "Allah sends the wind, and it carries the water and fertilizes the clouds with it, so they yield milk as a she-camel yields milk, and then it rains."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azamah related something similar from Ibn Abbas.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related from Ubayd ibn Umayr, who said: "Allah sends the bearers of glad tidings (al-mubashshirah), and they sweep over the earth with a sweep. Then He sends the stirrers (al-muthirah), which stir up the clouds and make them into fragments (kisaf). Then He sends the gatherers (al-mu'allifah), which gather them together and make them a heap (rukam). Then He sends the fertilizers (al-lawaqih), which fertilize them, and it rains."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azamah, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Daylami related with a weak chain from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The southern wind is from Paradise, and it is the fertilizing wind which Allah mentioned in His Book."

al-Tayalisi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Hibban, al-Tabarani and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, related from Ibn Abbas, who said: "A woman used to pray behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), a beautiful one among the most beautiful of women. Some of the people would advance so as to be in the first row, lest they see her, and some would hold back so as to be in the last row. When she bowed, they would look from beneath their armpits. So Allah revealed: ﴿And We have certainly known those who go before among you, and We have certainly known those who remain behind﴾." This hadith is from the narration of Abu al-Jawza' from Ibn Abbas.

Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn al-Mundhir related it as a statement of Abu al-Jawza'. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is more likely to be the sound (asahh)."

Ibn Kathir said: "In this hadith there is a severe irregularity (nakarah shadidah)."

al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, that he said: ﴿Those who go before﴾ are the earlier rows, and ﴿those who remain behind﴾ are the later rows.

Many hadiths have been reported that the best rows of men are the first of them and the worst are the last of them, and the best rows of women are the last of them and the worst are the first of them.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ata' and Muqatil ibn Hibban that the verse concerns the rows in battle.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Hasan, who said: "Those who go before in obedience to Allah, and those who remain behind in disobedience to Allah."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Abbas, who said: By "those who go before" is meant whoever has died, and by "those who remain behind" is meant whoever is alive and has not died.

These same (narrators) related from him also, who said: "Those who go before" are Adam and whoever passed on from his descendants, and "those who remain behind" are those still in the loins of men.

Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Qatadah something similar.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (*Fath al-Qadir*) on surah 15, verses 16–44 (part 1 of 2):

When He, glorified is He, mentioned the disbelief of the disbelievers and the incapacity of them and of their idols, He mentioned His dazzling power and His wondrous creation, so that they might infer His oneness from it. So He said: ﴿And We have certainly placed in the sky constellations of stars﴾. The verb *ja'ala* (placed/made) — if it means *khalaqa* (created), then *fi al-sama'* (in the sky) is connected to it; if it means *sayyara* (rendered, made into), then *fi al-sama'* is its predicate. *Al-buruj* (the constellations/mansions) in the language means palaces and dwellings, and what is meant here are the mansions of the sun, the moon and the wandering stars, which are the well-known twelve, as experience indicates. The Arabs consider knowledge of the positions of the stars and their mansions to be among the most noble sciences, and they use them to find their way, to know the times, and to know fertility and drought. They said: the celestial sphere has twelve *burj*s, and the names of these *buruj* are: Aries (*al-Hamal*), Taurus (*al-Thawr*), Gemini (*al-Jawza'*), Cancer (*al-Saratan*), Leo (*al-Asad*), Virgo (*al-Sunbulah*), Libra (*al-Mizan*), Scorpio (*al-'Aqrab*), Sagittarius (*al-Qaws*), Capricorn (*al-Jady*), Aquarius (*al-Dalw*), Pisces (*al-Hut*).

Each three of them are of the nature of one of the four elements, among those who occupy themselves with this science. They call Aries, Leo and Sagittarius the "fiery trigon"; Taurus, Virgo and Capricorn the "earthy trigon"; Gemini, Libra and Aquarius the "airy trigon"; and Cancer, Scorpio and Pisces the "watery trigon."

The root of *al-buruj* is *al-zuhur* (manifestation), and from it comes *tabarruj al-mar'ah* (a woman's displaying of her adornment).

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: *al-buruj* are the stars, and they were so called because of their manifestness and their elevation. It was also said: they are the seven wandering stars among them; this was said by Abu Salih. It was also said: they are palaces and houses in the sky, in which there are guards. The pronoun in *wa-zayyannaha* (and We adorned it) refers to the sky; that is, and We adorned the sky with the sun, the moon, the stars and the constellations, for the onlookers who look at it, or for the reflecting, heedful ones who infer, if it is from *al-nazar*, which is inference.

﴿And We guarded it﴾, that is, the sky, ﴿from every accursed devil﴾. Abu 'Ubaydah said: *al-rajim* means the one stoned with stars, as in His saying: ﴿missiles against the devils﴾ [al-Mulk: 5]. *Al-rajm* in the language is throwing stones; then it was used for cursing, expelling and distancing, *rajm*, because throwing stones entails these meanings.

﴿Except one who steals a hearing﴾. This is an exception that is *muttasil* (connected), that is, except from among those who steal a hearing. It may also be *munqati'* (disconnected), that is, but whoever steals a hearing, then a clear flaming fire pursues him. The meaning: We guarded the sky from the devils, so that they would not hear anything of the revelation or other things, except that one who steals a hearing, then the meteors pursue him and kill him or harm him. The meaning of *fa-atba'ahu* is that he followed him, overtook him, or caught up with him.

*Al-shihab* is the star or the blazing, shining fire, as in His saying: ﴿with a burning brand﴾ [al-Naml: 7]. Dhu al-Rummah said:

*"As if it were a star in pursuit of a demon."*

The star was called *shihab* because of its brightness, resembling fire. *Al-mubin* means evident to those who see; they see it and it is not obscured to them.

Al-Qurtubi said: It has been disputed whether the *shihab* kills or not. Ibn 'Abbas said: the *shihab* wounds, burns and harms, but does not kill. Al-Hasan and a group said: it kills.

Based on this view, regarding their being killed by the meteors before they have conveyed the hearing to the jinn, there are two opinions. The first: they are killed before they pass on to others what they have stolen by hearing, so the news of the heavens does not reach anyone other than the prophets; and for this reason soothsaying has ceased.

The second: they are killed after they have passed on what they stole by hearing to other jinn. He said: Al-Mawardi mentioned this, then said: the first view is more sound.

He said: It has been disputed whether there was hurling of meteors before the mission (*al-mab'ath*). Most said: yes. It was said: no, rather that happened only after the mission.

Al-Zajjaj said: The hurling of meteors is one of the signs of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, among the things that happened after his birth, because the poets in ancient times did not mention it in their poetry.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: *lawaqih* means *malaqih*; he went to the view that it is the plural of *malqahah*.

In this verse there is a comparison of the winds that carry water to a pregnant woman, and of the fertilization of trees to the impregnation of a pregnancy.

﴿And We sent down from the sky water﴾, that is, from the clouds. Everything that is above you and shades you is *sama'* (sky). It was also said: from the direction of the sky. The water here means rain water. ﴿And We gave it to you to drink﴾, that is, We made that rain for your watering, and for the drinking of your livestock and your land. Abu 'Ali said: one says *saqaytuhu al-ma'* when you give him an amount that quenches his thirst, and *asqaytuhu nahran*, that is, you made it a drinking place for him. On this basis, *asqaynakumuhu* is more emphatic than *saqaynakumuhu*. It was also said: *saqa* and *asqa* have one meaning. ﴿And you are not its keepers﴾, that is, its treasuries are not with you; rather its treasuries are with Us, and We are the keepers of it. Thus He, glorified is He, negated from them what He had affirmed for Himself in His saying: ﴿And there is not a thing but that with Us are its treasuries﴾. It was also said: the meaning is: you are not its keepers after We have sent it down upon you, that is, you cannot preserve it in wells, pools and springs; rather We are the ones who preserve it therein, so that it may be a store for you when you are in need of it.

﴿And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death﴾, that is, We bring life into existence in created beings and strip it from them whenever We wish. The purpose of this is to infer from these matters the perfection of His power, mighty and majestic is He, and that He is capable of resurrection, rising, and recompense to His servants according to what they deserve and what His will requires. For this reason He said: ﴿And We are the inheritors﴾, that is, of the earth and of whoever is upon it, because He, glorified is He, is the one who remains after the perishing of His creation, the Living who does not die, the Everlasting whose existence does not cease. ﴿And to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth﴾ [Al 'Imran: 180].

﴿And We have certainly known those who precede among you﴾. This *lam* is the one preparing for an oath (*al-lam al-muwatti'ah lil-qasam*), and likewise the *lam* in ﴿And We have certainly known those who delay﴾. What is meant by those who precede is those who precede in birth and death, and those who delay in them. It was said: those who precede in obedience and those who delay in it. It was said: those who precede in the battle line and those who delay. It was said: what is meant by those who precede are the dead, and by those who delay are the living. It was said: those who precede are the earlier nations before the community of Muhammad, and those who delay are the community of Muhammad. It was said: those who precede are those who were killed in jihad, and those who delay are those who were not killed.

﴿And indeed your Lord — it is He who will gather them﴾, that is, He is the one who takes charge of that, the one capable of it, to the exclusion of others, as the pronoun of separation (*damir al-fasl*) indicates by way of restriction. In it is [the indication] that He, glorified is He, will recompense the doer of good for his goodness and the doer of evil for his evil, because this is the very purpose of gathering. ﴿Indeed, He is Wise﴾, who conducts affairs according to what His far-reaching wisdom requires. ﴿Knowing﴾, whose knowledge encompasses all things, nothing being hidden from Him of them; and whoever is so, has far-reaching power over everything within the scope of His knowledge, (p-760) and His judgment proceeds in it, glorified is He; there is no god but Him.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿And We have certainly placed in the sky constellations of stars﴾, that he said: "Stars."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah the same (as above).

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Abu Salih, who said: "The great stars."

He also related from Atiyyah, who said: "Palaces in the sky, in which are the guards."

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Qatadah: "al-Rajim (the accursed one): the one cursed."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Except one who steals a hearing﴾, that he meant he wished to snatch the hearing, like His saying: ﴿Except one who snatches a snatching﴾ [al-Saffat: 10].

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Dahhak, who said: Ibn Abbas used to say that the shooting stars do not kill, but they burn, cause insanity (yakhbil) and wound, without killing.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from him regarding His saying: ﴿And We caused to grow therein of every thing weighed (mawzun)﴾, that he said: "Known (ma'lum)."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also, regarding ﴿of every thing weighed﴾, he said: "By measure (bi-qadar)."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Zayd, who said: "The things that are weighed."

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ikrimah, who said: "What the mountains cause to grow, like kohl and its like."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿And whom you are not providing for (lahu bi-raziqin)﴾, that he said: "The beasts and the livestock."

These same (narrators) related from Mansur, who said: "The wild animals."

al-Bazzar, Ibn Mardawayh and Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azamah related from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The treasuries of Allah are speech; when He wills a thing, He says to it 'Be,' and it is."

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn Jurayj regarding His saying: ﴿But with Us are its treasuries﴾, that he said: "Rain specifically."

Ibn al-Mundhir related from Mujahid something similar.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Rain has not decreased since Allah sent it down, but one land receives more rain than another," then he recited: ﴿And We do not send it down except in a known measure﴾.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "No year is rainier than another year, but Allah turns it wherever He wills," then he recited: ﴿And there is not a thing but its treasuries are with Us, and We do not send it down except in a known measure﴾.

Ibn Mardawayh related it from him as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) report.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Tabarani related from Ibn Mas'ud regarding His saying: ﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing (lawaqih)﴾, that he said: "Allah sends the wind, and it carries the water and fertilizes the clouds with it, so they yield milk as a she-camel yields milk, and then it rains."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azamah related something similar from Ibn Abbas.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related from Ubayd ibn Umayr, who said: "Allah sends the bearers of glad tidings (al-mubashshirah), and they sweep over the earth with a sweep. Then He sends the stirrers (al-muthirah), which stir up the clouds and make them into fragments (kisaf). Then He sends the gatherers (al-mu'allifah), which gather them together and make them a heap (rukam). Then He sends the fertilizers (al-lawaqih), which fertilize them, and it rains."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azamah, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Daylami related with a weak chain from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The southern wind is from Paradise, and it is the fertilizing wind which Allah mentioned in His Book."

al-Tayalisi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Hibban, al-Tabarani and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, related from Ibn Abbas, who said: "A woman used to pray behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), a beautiful one among the most beautiful of women. Some of the people would advance so as to be in the first row, lest they see her, and some would hold back so as to be in the last row. When she bowed, they would look from beneath their armpits. So Allah revealed: ﴿And We have certainly known those who go before among you, and We have certainly known those who remain behind﴾." This hadith is from the narration of Abu al-Jawza' from Ibn Abbas.

Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn al-Mundhir related it as a statement of Abu al-Jawza'. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is more likely to be the sound (asahh)."

Ibn Kathir said: "In this hadith there is a severe irregularity (nakarah shadidah)."

al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse, that he said: ﴿Those who go before﴾ are the earlier rows, and ﴿those who remain behind﴾ are the later rows.

Many hadiths have been reported that the best rows of men are the first of them and the worst are the last of them, and the best rows of women are the last of them and the worst are the first of them.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ata' and Muqatil ibn Hibban that the verse concerns the rows in battle.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Hasan, who said: "Those who go before in obedience to Allah, and those who remain behind in disobedience to Allah."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Abbas, who said: By "those who go before" is meant whoever has died, and by "those who remain behind" is meant whoever is alive and has not died.

These same (narrators) related from him also, who said: "Those who go before" are Adam and whoever passed on from his descendants, and "those who remain behind" are those still in the loins of men.

Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Qatadah something similar.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (*Fath al-Qadir*) on surah 15, verses 16–44 (part 1 of 2):

When He, glorified is He, mentioned the disbelief of the disbelievers and the incapacity of them and of their idols, He mentioned His dazzling power and His wondrous creation, so that they might infer His oneness from it. So He said: ﴿And We have certainly placed in the sky constellations of stars﴾. The verb *ja'ala* (placed/made) — if it means *khalaqa* (created), then *fi al-sama'* (in the sky) is connected to it; if it means *sayyara* (rendered, made into), then *fi al-sama'* is its predicate. *Al-buruj* (the constellations/mansions) in the language means palaces and dwellings, and what is meant here are the mansions of the sun, the moon and the wandering stars, which are the well-known twelve, as experience indicates. The Arabs consider knowledge of the positions of the stars and their mansions to be among the most noble sciences, and they use them to find their way, to know the times, and to know fertility and drought. They said: the celestial sphere has twelve *burj*s, and the names of these *buruj* are: Aries (*al-Hamal*), Taurus (*al-Thawr*), Gemini (*al-Jawza'*), Cancer (*al-Saratan*), Leo (*al-Asad*), Virgo (*al-Sunbulah*), Libra (*al-Mizan*), Scorpio (*al-'Aqrab*), Sagittarius (*al-Qaws*), Capricorn (*al-Jady*), Aquarius (*al-Dalw*), Pisces (*al-Hut*).

Each three of them are of the nature of one of the four elements, among those who occupy themselves with this science. They call Aries, Leo and Sagittarius the "fiery trigon"; Taurus, Virgo and Capricorn the "earthy trigon"; Gemini, Libra and Aquarius the "airy trigon"; and Cancer, Scorpio and Pisces the "watery trigon."

The root of *al-buruj* is *al-zuhur* (manifestation), and from it comes *tabarruj al-mar'ah* (a woman's displaying of her adornment).

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: *al-buruj* are the stars, and they were so called because of their manifestness and their elevation. It was also said: they are the seven wandering stars among them; this was said by Abu Salih. It was also said: they are palaces and houses in the sky, in which there are guards. The pronoun in *wa-zayyannaha* (and We adorned it) refers to the sky; that is, and We adorned the sky with the sun, the moon, the stars and the constellations, for the onlookers who look at it, or for the reflecting, heedful ones who infer, if it is from *al-nazar*, which is inference.

﴿And We guarded it﴾, that is, the sky, ﴿from every accursed devil﴾. Abu 'Ubaydah said: *al-rajim* means the one stoned with stars, as in His saying: ﴿missiles against the devils﴾ [al-Mulk: 5]. *Al-rajm* in the language is throwing stones; then it was used for cursing, expelling and distancing, *rajm*, because throwing stones entails these meanings.

﴿Except one who steals a hearing﴾. This is an exception that is *muttasil* (connected), that is, except from among those who steal a hearing. It may also be *munqati'* (disconnected), that is, but whoever steals a hearing, then a clear flaming fire pursues him. The meaning: We guarded the sky from the devils, so that they would not hear anything of the revelation or other things, except that one who steals a hearing, then the meteors pursue him and kill him or harm him. The meaning of *fa-atba'ahu* is that he followed him, overtook him, or caught up with him.

*Al-shihab* is the star or the blazing, shining fire, as in His saying: ﴿with a burning brand﴾ [al-Naml: 7]. Dhu al-Rummah said:

*"As if it were a star in pursuit of a demon."*

The star was called *shihab* because of its brightness, resembling fire. *Al-mubin* means evident to those who see; they see it and it is not obscured to them.

Al-Qurtubi said: It has been disputed whether the *shihab* kills or not. Ibn 'Abbas said: the *shihab* wounds, burns and harms, but does not kill. Al-Hasan and a group said: it kills.

Based on this view, regarding their being killed by the meteors before they have conveyed the hearing to the jinn, there are two opinions. The first: they are killed before they pass on to others what they have stolen by hearing, so the news of the heavens does not reach anyone other than the prophets; and for this reason soothsaying has ceased.

The second: they are killed after they have passed on what they stole by hearing to other jinn. He said: Al-Mawardi mentioned this, then said: the first view is more sound.

He said: It has been disputed whether there was hurling of meteors before the mission (*al-mab'ath*). Most said: yes. It was said: no, rather that happened only after the mission.

Al-Zajjaj said: The hurling of meteors is one of the signs of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, among the things that happened after his birth, because the poets in ancient times did not mention it in their poetry.

Many of the people of knowledge said: we see the shooting of stars, so it is possible that this is as we see it; then it becomes fire when it overtakes the devil. It is also possible to say that they are pelted with a flame of fire of the air, and so it appears to us that it is a star that is gliding.

﴿And the earth — We spread it out﴾, that is, We stretched it out and laid it out flat, as in His saying: ﴿and the earth, after that, He spread it out﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 30], and in His saying: ﴿and We laid out the earth, and how excellent are the Spreaders﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 48]. In this there is a refutation of whoever claims that it is like a sphere. ﴿And We cast into it firm mountains﴾, that is, mountains firmly fixed, lest it shake with its inhabitants. The explanation of this has already been given in surah al-Ra'd. ﴿And We caused to grow in it of everything weighed﴾, that is, We caused to grow in the earth of everything determined and known. He expressed this by *al-wazn* (weighing), because it is a measure by which things are known. From this is the saying of the poet:

*"Before your meeting I was one of strength; for every adversary, his balance is with me."*

It was also said: the meaning of *mawzun* is divided (*maqsum*); it was also said: counted (*ma'dud*). The intended purpose of the affirmation is origination and bringing into existence. It was also said: the pronoun refers to the mountains; that is, We caused to grow in the mountains of everything weighed: of gold, silver, copper, lead and the like. It was also said: *mawzun* is weighed by the balance of wisdom and determined by the measure of need. It was also said: *al-mawzun* is that whose goodness is judged, as one says *kalam mawzun*, that is, good speech.

﴿And We made for you therein means of livelihood﴾, by which you live, of foods and drinks; *ma'ayish* is the plural of *ma'isha*. It was said: they are garments. It was said: they are the management of the causes of provision for the duration of life. Al-Mawardi said: this is the apparent meaning.

I say: rather the first view is more apparent. From this is the saying of Jarir:

*"You burden me with the livelihood of the family of Zayd, and who for me [will provide] the thin bread and the lizard?"*

﴿And [also] those for whom you are not providers﴾ is coordinated with *ma'ayish* (means of livelihood); that is, We made for you therein means of livelihood, and [We made therein] for those for whom you are not providers: they are the slaves, the servants and the children, whose true provider is Allah, even if some of the servants think that he is the provider for them by virtue of his independent earning. It is also permissible for it to be coordinated with the position (*mahall*) of *lakum* (for you); that is, We made for you therein means of livelihood, and We made for those for whom you are not providers therein means of livelihood, and these are those previously mentioned, and this includes the animals of various kinds. It is not permissible to coordinate with the pronoun in *lakum* in the genitive, because according to most grammarians it is not permissible except by repeating the preposition. It was also said: he meant the wild animals.

﴿And there is not a thing but that with Us are its treasuries﴾. *In* (إن) is the negating particle, and *min* (مِن) is extra for emphasis. This construction is general, because an indefinite noun falls within the scope of negation together with the addition of *min*, and with the word *shay'* (thing), which encompasses all existents and applies to each individual among them. Thus it conveys that all things are, with Allah, in His treasuries; nothing goes out of them. *Al-khaza'in* is the plural of *khizanah*, which is the place in which precious things are kept. The mention of treasuries is an illustration of His capacity over every possible thing. The meaning: all possibilities are within His power and under His possession, which He brings from non-existence into existence in a measure as He wills.

Most of the exegetes said: what is meant in this verse is rain, because it is the cause of provisions and livelihoods. It was said: *al-khaza'in* are the keys; that is, there is not a thing but that with Us in the sky are its keys. The better view is what we have mentioned, namely the generality for every existent; indeed the word *shay'* may apply to the non-existent, according to the well-known disagreement on this matter.

﴿And We do not send it down except in a known measure﴾, that is, We do not send it down from the sky to the earth, or bring it into existence for the servants, except in a known measure. *Al-qadar* means the quantity. The meaning: Allah, glorified is He, does not bring into existence for the servants any of those things mentioned except accompanied by that bringing-into-existence in a specific measure, according to what His will requires, in proportion to the servants' need for it, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And if Allah had extended provision for His servants, they would have transgressed in the earth; but He sends down in measure what He wills﴾ [al-Shura: 27]. The sending down has been explained as giving, and explained as creating, and explained as bringing into existence; the meanings are close. The clause ﴿and We do not send it down﴾ is coordinated with an implied clause, that is: and there is not a thing but with Us are its treasuries, We send it down, and We do not send it down, or it is in the position of an accusative of circumstance (*hal*).

﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing﴾ is coordinated with ﴿And We made for you therein means of livelihood﴾, and what is between them is a parenthetical insertion.

Hamzah read *al-rih* (the wind) in the singular. The others read *al-riyah* (the winds) in the plural. On the reading of Hamzah, the definite article in *al-rih* is for the category (*li-l-jins*).

Al-Azhari said: He made the winds *lawaqih* (fertilizing) because they carry the clouds, that is, they bear them and turn them, then they pass over with them and cause them to descend. Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿until, when they have borne heavy clouds﴾ [al-A'raf: 57], that is, carried them. A she-camel is *laqih* when she has conceived the fetus in her womb. Al-Farra' and Ibn Qutaybah said this. It was also said: *lawaqih* means *mulaqqihah* (causing to fertilize). Ibn al-Anbari said: the Arabs say *abqala al-nabt fa-huwa baqil*, that is, *mubqil* (the plant has put forth green growth, so it is a green plant). The meaning: they fertilize the trees, that is, by their power. It was also said: the meaning of *lawaqih* is "possessing fertilization" (*dhawat laqah*). Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is "and possessing a bearing-state" (*dhat liqhah*), because they squeeze the clouds and milk them as a milk-camel is milked. Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Rain has not decreased since Allah sent it down, but one land receives more rain than another," then he recited: ﴿And We do not send it down except in a known measure﴾.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "No year is rainier than another year, but Allah turns it wherever He wills," then he recited: ﴿And there is not a thing but its treasuries are with Us, and We do not send it down except in a known measure﴾.

Ibn Mardawayh related it from him as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) report.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Tabarani related from Ibn Mas'ud regarding His saying: ﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing (lawaqih)﴾, that he said: "Allah sends the wind, and it carries the water and fertilizes the clouds with it, so they yield milk as a she-camel yields milk, and then it rains."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azamah related something similar from Ibn Abbas.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related from Ubayd ibn Umayr, who said: "Allah sends the bearers of glad tidings (al-mubashshirah), and they sweep over the earth with a sweep. Then He sends the stirrers (al-muthirah), which stir up the clouds and make them into fragments (kisaf). Then He sends the gatherers (al-mu'allifah), which gather them together and make them a heap (rukam). Then He sends the fertilizers (al-lawaqih), which fertilize them, and it rains."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azamah, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Daylami related with a weak chain from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The southern wind is from Paradise, and it is the fertilizing wind which Allah mentioned in His Book."

Some of the people would advance so as to be in the first row, lest they see her, and some would hold back so as to be in the last row. When she bowed, they would look from beneath their armpits. So Allah revealed: ﴿And We have certainly known those who go before among you, and We have certainly known those who remain behind﴾." Ibn Kathir said: "In this hadith there is a severe irregularity (nakarah shadidah)."

Many hadiths have been reported that the best rows of men are the first of them and the worst are the last of them, and the best rows of women are the last of them and the worst are the first of them.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ata' and Muqatil ibn Hibban that the verse concerns the rows in battle.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Hasan, who said: "Those who go before in obedience to Allah, and those who remain behind in disobedience to Allah."
