It has been said that the intended meaning is their questioning about the word of tawhid (monotheism).

The generality in ﴿about what they used to do﴾ indicates something wider than that. It has been said that those questioned here are all of the believers, the disobedient, and the disbelievers. This is indicated by His words: ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾ [al-Takathur: 8], and His words: ﴿Stop them, for they are to be questioned﴾ [al-Saffat: 24], and His words: ﴿Indeed, to Us is their return; then indeed, upon Us is their reckoning﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 25–26]. It may be said that restricting this questioning to those mentioned in the context and directing the generality toward them does not preclude the questioning of others.

﴿So proclaim what you are commanded﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: It means "make apparent what you are commanded," taken from *al-sadi'*, which is the dawn. End of quote.

The origin of *al-sadʿ* is separating and splitting. It is said: "I split it, and it split," i.e., it broke open; and "the people scattered" (*tasaddaʿa*), i.e., they dispersed. From this is ﴿On that Day they will be separated﴾ [al-Rum: 43], i.e., they will disperse.

Al-Farra' said: He meant "proclaim the matter," i.e., make your religion apparent, so *ma* with the verb is in this case like a verbal noun (*masdar*). Ibn al-Aʿrabi said: The meaning of *isdaʿ bi-ma tuʾmar* is: "aim (direct yourself)." It has been said: ﴿So proclaim what you are commanded﴾, i.e., divide their assembly and their word by calling them to tawhid, for they will scatter. The preferable view is that *sadʿ* means making apparent, as al-Zajjaj, al-Farra' and others said.

The grammarians said: The meaning is "by what you are commanded with of the laws," and they permitted that *ma* be a verbal (*masdariyyah*) particle, i.e., "by your command and your affair."

Al-Wahidi said: The exegetes said: That is, "proclaim the matter," i.e., your command, after making the call public. The Prophet (ﷺ) had remained hidden until this verse was revealed.

Then, after His command to proclaim, the Exalted commanded him to turn away and not to pay attention to the polytheists, saying: ﴿And turn away from the polytheists﴾, i.e., do not care about them and do not turn to them if they blame you for making the call public.

Then He confirmed this command and strengthened the heart of His Messenger, saying: ﴿Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers﴾, even though they were among the great disbelievers and people of power among them. If Allah suffices him against their affair by suppressing and destroying them, He will suffice him against the affair of those who are lower than them, all the more so. These mockers were five of the chiefs of the people of Makkah: al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il, al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib ibn al-Harith ibn Zamʿah, al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghuth, and al-Harith ibn al-Tulatilah.

Thus said al-Qurtubi, and other exegetes concurred with him.

Allah destroyed them all and sufficed him against their affair in a single day.

Then He described these mockers with polytheism, saying: ﴿Those who set up another god with Allah﴾. So their sin was not merely mockery; rather, they had another sin, which is polytheism against Allah, glorified is He. Then He threatened them, saying: ﴿But they are going to know﴾, how their end will be in the Hereafter and what of the punishment of Allah, glorified is He, will befall them.

Then He mentioned another consolation for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), after the first consolation, by sufficing him against their evil and repelling their plotting. He said: ﴿And We certainly know that your breast becomes constricted by what they say﴾, from the disbelieving statements that include slander against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) by saying he is a sorcerer, a madman, a soothsayer, and a liar. Such things did occur with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in accordance with human nature and the human temperament.

Then He, glorified is He, commanded him to turn, to relieve the distress of the constriction of the breast, to the glorification of Allah, glorified is He, and His praise. He said: ﴿So glorify with the praise of your Lord﴾, meaning: while clothed in His praise; that is, perform the glorification accompanied by praise. ﴿And be among those who prostrate﴾, meaning: those who pray. For when you do that, Allah will relieve your concern, remove your grief, and expand your breast.

Then He commanded him to worship his Lord, that is, to persist in it until a limit, which is His saying: ﴿until there comes to you the certainty﴾, meaning death.

Al-Wahidi said: The company of exegetes said: it means death, because he is certain of it.

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is "worship your Lord forever," because if it were said "worship your Lord" without a time limit, it would be permissible for a person, once he had worshipped once, to be considered obedient. But when He says ﴿until there comes to you the certainty﴾, He has commanded him to persist in worship forever, for as long as he is alive.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Umar, regarding His saying ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated﴾, that he said: "The seven oft-repeated is the Opening of the Book (al-Fatihah)."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Daraqutni, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi related the same from Ali through multiple chains.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh related the same from Ibn Mas'ud, and added: "And the Great Qur'an is the rest of the Qur'an."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi related from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse that he said: "The Opening of the Book, which Allah singled out for the community of Muhammad, raised it in the Mother of the Book, and kept it in store for them until He brought it out, and it was not given to anyone before." It was asked: "Then where is the seventh verse?" He said: ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾. Similar to this was related from him through several chains.

Ibn al-Durays, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh related from Abu Hurayrah who said: "The seven oft-repeated is the Opening of the Book."

Ibn Jarir related from Ubayy ibn Ka'b who said: "The seven oft-repeated is ﴿Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾."

Something similar to the statement of these Companions was related from a group of the Successors.

It is established in Sahih al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id ibn al-Mu'alla, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Shall I teach you the best surah before I leave the mosque?" The Prophet (ﷺ) then went to leave, and I reminded him, and he said: ﴿Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Fatihah: 1], it is the seven oft-repeated and the Great Qur'an.

Al-Bukhari also related from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Mother of the Qur'an is the seven oft-repeated and the Great Qur'an." Therefore, by this it is necessary to conclude that it is the Opening of the Book. However, naming it thus does not negate naming something else with it, as we have previously mentioned.

Ibn Mardawayh related from Umar, regarding the verse, that he said: "It is the seven long surahs."

Ibn Jarir related the same from Ibn Mas'ud.

Al-Firyabi, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi related from Ibn Abbas that he said regarding the verse: "It is the seven long surahs."

Al-Darimi and Ibn Mardawayh related the same from Ubayy ibn Ka'b.

Something similar to this was related from a group of the Successors.

Ibn Mardawayh related through the chain of Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas who said: "It is the Opening of the Book and the seven long surahs."

Ibn Jarir related from him regarding the verse that he said: "It is what is repeated from the Qur'an. Have you not heard the saying of Allah: ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement, a Book consistent, its parts repeating (mathani)﴾ [al-Zumar: 23]?"

Ibn Jarir related from al-Dahhak who said: "The mathani is the Qur'an, in which Allah mentions one story many times."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi related from Ziyad ibn Abi Maryam regarding the verse that he said: "I gave you seven parts: command, prohibit, give good news, warn, strike examples, count the blessings, and recite the report of the Qur'an."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿Do not extend your eyes﴾ that he said: "He forbade the man from wishing for the wealth of his companion."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Mujahid regarding His saying ﴿pairs of them﴾ that he said: "The rich are the likes and the similars."

Ibn al-Mundhir related from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah who said: "Whoever is given the Qur'an and then stretches his eye toward something that the Qur'an has belittled has opposed the Qur'an. Has he not heard His saying: ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated﴾, and His saying: ﴿And the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting﴾ [Ta-Ha: 131]?" Ibn Uyaynah also explained the sound hadith "He is not of us who does not beautify his voice with the Qur'an" by saying: the meaning is "he who does not find sufficiency in it."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His saying ﴿and lower your wing﴾ that he said: "Humble yourself."

Al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, al-Bukhari, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, and Ibn Mardawayh related through several chains from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿as We sent down upon the dividers﴾, the verse, that he said: "They are the People of the Book, who divided it into parts, believing in some of it and disbelieving in some of it."

Ibn Jarir related through the chain of Ali ibn Abi Talhah from him that he said: "ʿIḍīn means groups."

Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Nu'aym, and al-Bayhaqi related from Ibn Abbas that it was revealed concerning a group of the Quraysh who used to turn people away from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), among them al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah.

al-Tirmidhi, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Anas, "from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding His saying ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all about what they used to do﴾, that he said: 'About the statement: there is no god but Allah.'"

Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn al-Mundhir related it through another route from Anas as a statement of his own (mawquf).

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related the same from Ibn Umar.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim related through the chain of Ali ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿So proclaim what you are commanded﴾ that it means: carry it out. There is a well-known discussion concerning Ali ibn Abi Talhah.

Ibn Jarir related from Abu Ubaydah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) remained in hiding until ﴿So proclaim what you are commanded﴾ was revealed, and then he and his Companions came out."

Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Jarir related from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse that he said: "This is a command from Allah to His Prophet to convey his message to his people and to all whom he was sent to."

Ibn al-Mundhir related from him: ﴿So proclaim what you are commanded﴾, he said: "Make it public what you are commanded."

Abu Dawud in his book on abrogation (Nasikh) and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿And turn away from the polytheists﴾ that he said: "It was abrogated by His saying: ﴿Kill the polytheists﴾ [al-Tawbah: 5]."

al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym, and al-Diya' in al-Mukhtarah related from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers﴾ that he said: "The mockers were al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth, al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib, al-Harith ibn Aytal al-Sahmi, and al-As ibn Wa'il," and he mentioned the story of their destruction.

This was related from a group of the Companions, with additions and omissions in their number, and with considerable length regarding that.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim in al-Tarikh, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Daylami related from Abu Muslim al-Khawlani who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It was not revealed to me that I should gather wealth and be among the merchants; rather, it was revealed to me that ﴿Glorify with the praise of your Lord and be among the prostrators﴾ and ﴿Worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty﴾."

Ibn Mardawayh related the same from Ibn Mas'ud in a raised (marfu') form.

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Daylami related something similar from Abu al-Darda in a raised form.

al-Khatib in al-Muttafiq wal-Muftariq related through the chain of Ubayd Allah ibn Aban ibn Uthman ibn Hudhayfah ibn Aws al-Ta'ifi who said: Aban ibn Uthman narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather, who raised it, similar to the hadith of Abu Muslim al-Khawlani.

Ibn Abi Shaybah related from Salim ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar regarding ﴿until there comes to you the certainty﴾ that he said: "Death."

Ibn al-Mubarak related the same from al-Hasan.

Ibn Jarir related the same from Ibn Zayd.
